item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-7911fb68dd28a7b7","start_unit":7,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"In January 2023, Scholz stated that Germany had maintained energy supply after ending Russian gas, oil, and coal dependence by reopening coal plants, extending nuclear-plant use, filling gas storage, adding import routes and LNG terminals, and providing multibillion-euro energy-price relief; he also described continued plans to accelerate renewable-energy, grid, and industrial transformation.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.9","5B.10","6B.6","8B.2","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"January 2023; reports measures and claimed outcomes from the preceding energy crisis, with forward-looking plans for 2023 and beyond.","ruler_attribution":"Scholz attributed the decisions and outcomes to the Federal Government he led.","limitations":["The source is a government speech and does not independently verify the claimed outcomes or distributional effects.","It provides no detailed evidence of implementation quality beyond the measures described."]},{"source_id":"SRC-7911fb68dd28a7b7","start_unit":8,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"Scholz said Germany would continue supplying Ukraine with increasingly heavy weapons, including Leopard 2 tanks, while coordinating with allies, training Ukrainian crews, and providing logistics, ammunition, and maintenance; he explicitly framed the policy as supporting Ukraine's defence while preventing escalation into a NATO-Russia war and said decisions were taken incrementally because there were no mathematically certain choices.","question_ids":["1B.2","1B.5","1B.8","2B.5","2B.8","2B.10","8B.2","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"January 2023; describes decisions already taken and the intended 2023 policy posture.","ruler_attribution":"Scholz directly described and defended decisions by his government, including the Leopard 2 decision.","limitations":["The speech establishes stated policy and safeguards but does not independently establish whether escalation risks were actually reduced or whether supplied weapons were lawfully used."]},{"source_id":"SRC-ff17d4fc90370148","start_unit":24,"end_unit":25,"fact_summary":"On 29 March 2023, the Bundestag's official protocol recorded that, after Scholz's government questioning, parliament approved continued German participation in the NATO-led SEA GUARDIAN maritime security operation by 550 votes to 106, with two abstentions.","question_ids":["2B.1","2B.8","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"29 March 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The decision was made through the Bundestag following reporting by Chancellor Scholz; the protocol does not specify his individual vote or operational contribution.","limitations":["The supplied protocol records parliamentary approval but gives no substantive details about the mission's conduct, objectives, or civilian effects."]},{"source_id":"SRC-ffa5a98c7207485e","start_unit":5,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"At the Munich Security Conference in February 2023, Scholz stated that Germany had provided more than €12 billion to Ukraine in the prior year, admitted more than one million Ukrainian refugees with access to work, education, and universities, and supplied more military goods than any other continental European country; he defended continued support as compatible with pursuing an eventual Russian withdrawal and prosecuting war crimes.","question_ids":["2B.4","2B.5","2B.8","2B.9","2B.10","6B.3","6B.6","8B.3","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"17 February 2023; reports 2022 support and describes continuing policy.","ruler_attribution":"Scholz presented these measures as actions of the German Government.","limitations":["The speech does not independently verify the amounts, comparative ranking, refugee access in practice, or prosecution outcomes.","It provides no detailed arms-transfer monitoring or abuse-correction mechanism."]},{"source_id":"SRC-ffa5a98c7207485e","start_unit":6,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"Scholz said Germany would balance comprehensive, prolonged support for Ukraine with avoiding unintended escalation, coordinate key steps closely among allies, and maintain caution over hasty unilateral action; he linked this approach to successive deliveries of artillery, air defence, armoured vehicles, Patriot systems, and battle tanks.","question_ids":["1B.2","1B.8","2B.5","2B.7","2B.10","8B.5","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"17 February 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Scholz stated the policy and described decisions by the government he led.","limitations":["This is a stated crisis-management framework, not independent evidence of effectiveness or absence of escalation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-ffa5a98c7207485e","start_unit":7,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"Scholz stated that Germany had created a €100 billion Bundeswehr special fund through a Basic Law amendment, intended to rebuild military capability, and committed to permanently spending 2% of GDP on defence; he also described NATO readiness, additional deployments for Lithuania, air-defence assistance to Poland and Slovakia, and protection of North and Baltic Sea infrastructure.","question_ids":["1B.1","1B.3","2B.8","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"17 February 2023; describes enacted funding and planned implementation.","ruler_attribution":"Scholz attributed the constitutional amendment, fund, spending commitment, and deployments to his government and parliamentary majority.","limitations":["The source does not establish actual disbursement, procurement completion, readiness outcomes, or proportionality of the spending."]},{"source_id":"SRC-ffa5a98c7207485e","start_unit":8,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"Scholz said Germany had ended its dependence on Russian energy within twelve months, was diversifying suppliers and supply chains, strengthening semiconductor production, and seeking to include resilience objectives in its National Security Strategy.","question_ids":["1B.10","5B.3","5B.4","5B.10","8B.2","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"17 February 2023; reports actions during the preceding twelve months and future plans.","ruler_attribution":"Scholz attributed the energy and industrial-resilience measures to the German Government.","limitations":["The speech does not independently verify the claimed end of dependence or quantify costs and distributional effects."]},{"source_id":"SRC-25225c4337014d09","start_unit":24,"end_unit":25,"fact_summary":"In a February 2023 government declaration, Scholz defended confidential advance coordination with President Biden and allies before announcing tank decisions, said logistics and Ukrainian training were organized alongside deliveries, and announced further sanctions against Russia for the war's first anniversary.","question_ids":["2B.5","2B.6","2B.8","8B.5","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"8 February 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The Bundestag account attributes the declaration and announced policies to Chancellor Scholz and his government.","limitations":["The account does not detail the sanctions, their enforcement, or the transparency and oversight implications of confidential preparation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-224d63cffa60ed4a","start_unit":24,"end_unit":26,"fact_summary":"On 16 March 2023, Scholz said Germany was prepared to open its military procurement plans to other EU members to accelerate ammunition procurement for Ukraine, while continuing military support and sanctions against Russia; he also stated that Germany had become independent of Russian gas without freezing or suffering an economic collapse.","question_ids":["2B.5","2B.8","2B.10","5B.3","5B.9","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"16 March 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The Bundestag account attributes the procurement proposal, sanctions policy, and energy claims to Scholz's government.","limitations":["The source does not establish whether the procurement opening occurred, how much ammunition was obtained, or whether sanctions achieved their stated purpose.","The economic and energy claims are presented politically and include opposing parliamentary assessments."]},{"source_id":"SRC-fe34f2356e9cf242","start_unit":24,"end_unit":26,"fact_summary":"In a 29 March 2023 government questioning, Scholz identified accelerated planning and approval procedures for transport infrastructure, energy grids, and energy-generation facilities; he set a target of 15 million electric vehicles by 2030, supported annual climate-target review, proposed building-energy rules with multiple compliance pathways and funding, and described a planned skilled-worker immigration law.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.4","5B.6","5B.7","5B.10","6B.2","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"29 March 2023; records stated priorities, proposed legislation, and administrative plans.","ruler_attribution":"The Bundestag account attributes the priorities and commitments to Chancellor Scholz and his government.","limitations":["Several measures were announced or under preparation rather than shown as enacted and implemented.","The source does not provide outcome evidence for climate, infrastructure, immigration, or benefit-uptake goals."]},{"source_id":"SRC-fe34f2356e9cf242","start_unit":25,"end_unit":26,"fact_summary":"During the same 29 March questioning, Scholz said the child supplement reached only about 30% of eligible lower-income families, compared with full uptake of child benefit, and said the government needed to increase uptake; he also stated that Germany had received about one million Ukrainians, allocated €3.5 billion in 2022, and incurred €5 billion annually through citizen-benefit arrangements.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.3","6B.5","6B.6","6B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"29 March 2023; reports 2022 and current 2023 conditions and intended corrective action.","ruler_attribution":"Scholz supplied the figures and stated the government's intended response.","limitations":["The source does not explain the causes of low child-supplement uptake or show whether the proposed correction succeeded.","The refugee-cost figures are presented without independent verification or distributional analysis."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b00fe58bd66fb2bf","start_unit":24,"end_unit":25,"fact_summary":"On 2 March 2023, Scholz rejected a peace settlement negotiated over Ukrainians' heads, promised further arms deliveries in close coordination with partners, and said Germany would continue to ensure NATO did not become a party to the war; he also reaffirmed Germany's 2% GDP defence-spending commitment and promised to contract most of the €100 billion special fund during 2023.","question_ids":["1B.2","1B.8","2B.1","2B.5","2B.7","2B.8","2B.10","8B.2","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"2 March 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The Bundestag account attributes the positions and commitments to Chancellor Scholz.","limitations":["The account includes opposition claims that only €600 million had been spent from the fund and that the 2% target was not being met; these claims are not independently adjudicated in the supplied text.","No evidence is supplied about the success of diplomatic alternatives or the actual pace of contracting."]},{"source_id":"SRC-48a0822e1680094b","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"At the UN General Debate in September 2023, Scholz affirmed non-use of force, rejection of revisionism, inviolability of borders, and cooperation through the UN; he stated that Germany was the UN's second-largest regular-budget contributor and supported stronger representation for Africa, Asia, and Latin America in Security Council reform.","question_ids":["2B.1","2B.7","2B.10","8B.1","8B.9"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"19 September 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Scholz stated Germany's international commitments and policy positions.","limitations":["The speech records commitments and contribution claims but not their independent effects on conflict outcomes or institutional reform."]},{"source_id":"SRC-48a0822e1680094b","start_unit":6,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"Scholz stated that Germany had tripled international climate finance from more than €4 billion in 2020 to €6 billion in the previous year, was honouring its pledges, and supported binding renewable-energy and energy-efficiency targets; he also said Germany would provide €305 million in hybrid capital to the World Bank, expected to enable more than €2 billion in additional loans.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.10","6B.1","6B.6","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"19 September 2023; reports prior-year financing and current commitments.","ruler_attribution":"Scholz attributed the financing and reform support to Germany under his government.","limitations":["The source is a speech and does not independently verify the financing figures, additional-loan estimate, or resulting welfare and climate outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-48a0822e1680094b","start_unit":6,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"Scholz said Germany was actively fostering negotiations on a Global Digital Compact and argued for common rules governing possible use of generative artificial intelligence as a weapon, while warning that unequal access and biased algorithms could deepen global divisions.","question_ids":["1B.9","8B.1","8B.2","8B.9"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"19 September 2023; describes an international rule-making initiative in progress.","ruler_attribution":"Scholz stated Germany's diplomatic position and participation.","limitations":["The source reports advocacy and participation, not enacted German safeguards, funding, enforcement, or review mechanisms."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a9ed551f9515cbc0","start_unit":7,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"After the Federal Constitutional Court rejected the government's earlier interpretation of the constitutional debt-brake rules, Scholz said the government accepted that the Court had the last word, that political debate on the ruling was over, and that the government would revise its 2023 budget through a supplementary budget and comply with the Court's requirements.","question_ids":["4B.4","5B.3","5B.7","8B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"28 November 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Scholz acknowledged the constitutional ruling and described the government's corrective response.","limitations":["The speech does not independently assess the legality of the prior practice beyond reporting the Court's ruling or establish the eventual legislative outcome."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a9ed551f9515cbc0","start_unit":8,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"Following the court ruling, the government froze new spending from the Climate and Transformation Fund except for existing contractual commitments and selected building-efficiency and renewable-energy measures, proposed reducing the fund's 2023 reserve by €60 billion, deferred 2024 budget completion, and sought parliamentary authorization for energy-price relief and Ahr Valley flood assistance under the constitutional emergency provision.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.6","5B.7","5B.9","6B.6","8B.2","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"28 November 2023; describes immediate corrective measures and proposed budget actions.","ruler_attribution":"Scholz described decisions by the government and governing parliamentary factions.","limitations":["The source does not establish final parliamentary approval, subsequent implementation, or the effects of the €60 billion reduction.","The account is the Chancellor's own explanation of the response."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a9ed551f9515cbc0","start_unit":8,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"Scholz reported that Germany had built LNG terminals in record time, provided up to €200 billion during winter 2022 to protect households and companies from the energy shock, filled gas storage sufficiently to reduce expected price-spike risk, and planned to end energy-price brakes because prevailing tariffs were below their caps.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.9","5B.10","6B.6","8B.3","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"28 November 2023; reports 2022-2023 measures and current conditions.","ruler_attribution":"Scholz attributed the infrastructure, financial assistance, and storage decisions to his government.","limitations":["The speech does not independently verify the €200 billion amount, terminal completion, storage adequacy, or who benefited from the relief.","It does not provide a distributional assessment of the assistance."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a9ed551f9515cbc0","start_unit":8,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"Scholz stated that the government continued Ukraine support, including Germany's position as the second-largest supporter after the United States and as a major weapons provider, and had accepted more than one million Ukrainians in Germany; he linked these choices to European security and humanitarian responsibility.","question_ids":["2B.5","2B.8","2B.10","6B.3","6B.6","8B.3","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"28 November 2023; summarizes policy and support through 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Scholz attributed the support and reception policy to the government he led.","limitations":["The source does not independently verify comparative support rankings, reception outcomes, or arms-transfer controls."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a9ed551f9515cbc0","start_unit":8,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"Scholz stated that the government's longer-term program was to modernize infrastructure, transform the economy, advance the energy transition, resolve accumulated reform delays, and preserve competitiveness and future crisis capacity, while prioritizing security, climate neutrality, and social cohesion in the 2024 budget.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.10","6B.1","6B.9","8B.1","8B.2","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"28 November 2023; summarizes the government's program and budget priorities at period end.","ruler_attribution":"Scholz explicitly attributed the program to the government he led.","limitations":["This is primarily a programmatic statement and does not establish completed outcomes or durability by the end of 2023."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-56f14c4806425617","SRC-377194a96c595d3a"],"batch_limitations":["The supplied corpus consists primarily of official speeches, government summaries, and parliamentary web pages; it contains limited independent evaluation of implementation, outcomes, legality beyond the reported court ruling, or distributional effects.","The two supplied legal texts establish general assembly rights and penalties for unlawful assemblies but do not describe an action, policy, or institutional finding attributable to Scholz during 2023."]}
